findings.title: LDs calculated on contract value and exceed 5% cap
findings.deviation: Liquidated damages are calculated as 1% of the total Contract Value per week of delay (up to a 10% cap) instead of 0.5% of the affected milestone fee (up to 5%). Additionally, there is no carve-out for client-caused delay.
findings.impact: AtliQ could face disproportionate penalties calculated on the entire project value even for minor, milestone-specific delays, including those caused by the client.
findings.quote: 12.2 Should the Service Provider fail to achieve any Milestone by its scheduled completion date, the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay. 12.3 The aggregate liquidated damages payable under this Clause 12 shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Contract Value.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week of delay, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no liquidated damages where the delay is caused by the client; and liquidated damages shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Unlimited liability for data protection incidents
findings.deviation: Liability for data protection is excluded from the cap, creating unlimited liability for data incidents. Additionally, the cap is set at the total Contract Value rather than 1x fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces unlimited financial exposure in the event of any personal data incidents or unauthorized disclosures.
findings.quote: Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.
findings.counterPosition: Data protection liability should be capped, ideally under a separate, reasonable super-cap (e.g., 2x fees), rather than being entirely unlimited.

findings.title: No payment for work-in-progress on convenience termination
findings.deviation: On termination for convenience, AtliQ is only paid for services 'performed and accepted', which excludes work-in-progress and unaccepted deliverables.
findings.impact: AtliQ could perform substantial services but receive zero compensation for ongoing work if the client terminates for convenience before formal acceptance.
findings.quote: The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice, in which event the Company shall pay for all Services performed and accepted up to the date of termination.
findings.counterPosition: The Company must pay for all services performed up to the date of termination, including work in progress and any non-cancellable third-party committed costs.

findings.title: Restriction on hosting and offshore processing of guest data
findings.deviation: The contract requires all Guest Data to be hosted within Saudi Arabia and restricts transfer outside the Kingdom without prior written approval, which conflicts with AtliQ's offshore delivery model from India.
findings.impact: AtliQ's Indian team may be legally restricted from accessing, processing, or supporting the platform remotely unless written approval is secured upfront.
findings.quote: Guest Data shall be hosted within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia unless the Company provides prior written approval for any transfer outside the Kingdom.
findings.counterPosition: The parties should agree to a de-identified offshore access route or secure written approval for AtliQ's Indian entity (AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd) to access the data for support/development purposes upfront.

fine.note: Client owns deliverables only upon payment in full, and AtliQ retains background IP.
Indemnification is limited to standard IP infringement and materials, with no one-way or uncapped general indemnities.
Confidentiality obligations are mutual, balanced, and survive for a standard term.
The contract contains no non-compete or non-solicitation restrictions.
There are no onerous insurance requirements or cover limits imposed.
Right of deduction is limited strictly to liquidated damages under this agreement.
